items: ==Three-sided marketplace==: customers order, restaurants prepare, riders deliver
Platform earns a **15-25%** commission per order
{green:In scope}: discovery, cart, order, payment, dispatch, tracking, notifications
Ratings and refunds: light touches only
{red:Out of scope v1}: grocery quick-commerce, table booking, loyalty, ads auctions
End to end: about **30-40 min**
Most data and traffic are ==geo-partitioned by city==
Generic e-commerce design: ignores **perishable** food and the prep clock
Ignoring time-bound rider supply, so orders sit unassigned
Sizing for the average, not the 3-5x peak
Showing restaurants outside the 5-8 km radius
Drawing boxes before confirming scope

blocks.title: Interview opener
blocks.text: In the first 3-5 minutes, state assumptions out loud and confirm scope before drawing boxes.

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Customer: search, browse, view menus, manage a cart
Customer: place and pay, track live, cancel or refund, rate
Restaurant: accept/reject orders, update menu and stock
Rider: go online, accept a task, update status

blocks.title: 3. Sizing Flow
items: 50M MAU → 10M DAU → 3M orders/day
Orders: 3M ÷ 86,400 ≈ ==35 avg QPS==
5x peak factor ≈ ==175-200 orders/sec==
Browse: 30 per order, 90M/day ≈ 1,000 avg, 5,000 peak QPS
Riders: 500K × 1 ping/4 s ≈ ==125K writes/sec==

blocks.title: 6. Failure Scenarios
items: Orders, payments: {red:CP}, strongly consistent
Discovery, menus, ETA: AP, seconds stale is fine
Checkout never double-charges: **correctness** over availability
Mistake: averaging QPS over 24 h, not the 2-hour dinner peak

blocks.title: 7. Key Metrics
items: Browse is ==100:1== read-heavy: cache and replicas
Tracking is write-heavy: Kafka plus Redis
So the two paths scale separately
Downtime budget: ordering ≈ 22 min/month, browsing ≈ 43
Traffic spikes ==3-5x== at lunch (12-14h) and dinner (19-22h)
Size capacity for the **peak**, not the average
Rider supply is time-bound too, so dispatch peaks with orders
Non-critical traffic like marketing is shed first

blocks.title: Cheatsheet numbers
blocks.text: Peak 200 orders/s, 125K location writes/s, search p99 300 ms, 99.95% order availability.

items: Split the app into ==services== that scale on their own
Entry path: {icon:cloudfront} CDN → {icon:apigateway} API gateway (auth, rate limit, routing)
One **BFF** each for customer, restaurant and rider apps
Core: Catalog, Search, Cart, Order, Payment, Dispatch, Tracking, Notification, Pricing, User
Gateway authenticates and routes to the BFF
Cart is priced, then Order is created (sync gRPC)
Payment charges; emits `PaymentCaptured` to Kafka
Restaurant, Dispatch, Notification consume it (async)

blocks.text: User-facing calls use ==REST/gRPC==; cross-service events like `OrderPlaced` go through **Kafka**. Same key → same partition → per-key ordering.

items: CDN caches images and static menus
Redis caches hot restaurant lists, ==TTL 30-60 s==
Geo-sharding: each city is a cell with own order DB, dispatch, tracking
A failure stays inside **one city**

blocks.text: Browse runs at ==5K QPS==; tracking writes hit ==125K/s==. A monolith forces **one** scaling unit for both.

items: Each service gets its own autoscaling rule
Deploy one service without touching the rest
Tracking load never starves checkout
Sharing one database among services
Couples schemas, so every change needs joint deploys
One bad query slows every service
Fix: each service owns its data, others call its API or events
Each cell owns order DB, dispatch, tracking
Bad deploy hits roughly ==1-5%== of traffic
Roll out cell by cell, watch metrics between
Gateway → Cart → Order → Payment
PaymentCaptured event fans out via Kafka
Restaurant, Dispatch, Notification react in parallel
Sync path stays short; the rest is **async**
Gateway p99 added latency under 20 ms
Kafka consumer lag under 5 s on order-events
Cache hit ratio above 90% on restaurant lists

blocks.title: 12. Design Review Checks
items: Does each service own its own data?
Are events keyed to keep order?
Is a single city failure contained?
Is the cache TTL short enough?
Partition key is `order_id` or `rider_id`
Same key → same partition → ==per-key order==
Consumers are **idempotent**: replays are safe
Sync only where the user waits for an answer
Everything after PaymentCaptured is ==async==
A slow consumer never blocks checkout
One shared database across services
Designing a generic store, ignoring the prep clock
Sync calls chained through every service
Unkeyed events that arrive out of order
Timeouts on every call between services
Retries with ==jittered backoff==, never tight loops
**Circuit breakers** stop calls to a failing service
Bulkheads keep one slow path from eating all threads
Menu served from cache if Catalog is down
Search simplified when Elasticsearch struggles
Tracking falls back to ==status only==

blocks.title: 18. Observability
items: Golden-signals dashboard per service
Tracing with an `order_id` correlation
SLO alerts on order success rate
Alert on the stuck-order count
Reads: CDN images, Redis hot lists, ==Elasticsearch replicas==
Order history is served from **read replicas**
Writes: shard the orders DB by city or user
Partition Kafka topics by key
Location firehose runs in its own pipeline
Each step has an undo: refund, cancel rider
No two-phase commit across services
Outbox + idempotent consumers: ==effectively-once==

blocks.title: Interview Q: two orders, one rider?
blocks.text: Use an atomic lock or compare-and-set on the rider's state, plus an idempotent assignment.

blocks.title: Start hybrid
blocks.text: With 1-5 engineers use a modular monolith; split into microservices at 3M orders/day.

blocks.title: Interview tip
blocks.text: Name the scaling reason for each split: browse 5K QPS, tracking 125K writes/s.

items: List ==nearby open== restaurants for the user's location
Search by **dish**, cuisine or restaurant name
Filter and sort (rating, price, veg, ETA)
Personalise the order with an ML score
Encode lat/lng as ==geohash== 5 (~4.9 km); query cell + 8 neighbours (or S2/H3)
Keep only open places in the delivery polygon with rider supply, **not** distance alone
Match text with edge n-grams + fuzziness 1-2; suggest p99 < 100 ms
Rank: relevance, distance, rating, ETA, prep time, offers, ML score
Cache page 1 per (cell, filter) key in Redis, TTL 30-60 s
Open/closed and out-of-stock reach the index via CDC in ~5-10 s
An ==eventually consistent== index is accepted
Redis hit rate is about 70-80% on popular cells
Search is read-only: add **replicas**, shard the index by city

blocks.title: 7. Failure Scenarios
items: Elasticsearch down → serve cached last-known list per cell
Hide the filters while in fallback mode
Stale index → restaurant shown but gone: recheck at checkout

blocks.title: 8. Key Metrics
items: Search p99 latency (target < 300 ms)
Zero-result rate < 2%
Click-through rate on results
Index lag in seconds (target ~5-10 s)

blocks.title: 9. Mistake
blocks.text: Ranking only by distance buries high-rated restaurants. Showing out-of-stock items breaks trust.

items: Own the ==order lifecycle== from CREATED to DELIVERED
Be the **single** source of truth for order status
Emit an event on every transition (OrderPaid, OrderPicked...)
Side exits: **CANCELLED**, **REJECTED**, REFUNDED
Guarded: only ==legal edges== pass, via `UPDATE ... WHERE version = ?`
No reply from restaurant in **3 min**: auto-REJECT, refund, re-suggest
Shard by `user_id` or `city_id`: one customer's orders co-located
Peak is only ~200 TPS: the DB copes **easily**
Each shard: 1 primary + replicas
Cancel is **free** before the restaurant accepts
A partial fee applies after PREPARING
**No** cancel after PICKED_UP
Client sends an ==Idempotency-Key== header: a retried POST /orders returns the **same** order
Outbox: state change + event in one transaction, relay publishes to Kafka, nothing lost
Duplicate or out-of-order event: version checks, plus ==idempotent consumers==

blocks.title: 7. Key Metrics
items: Order success rate **above 98%**
Acceptance rate and cancellation rate
Time in each state
Stuck-order count
Zero rows changed: reload the order, then retry or reject
Every transition also appends an ==order_status_history== row
An illegal edge returns **409 Conflict**
Restaurant tablet gets the order the moment it is PAID
Silence for **3 min** counts as a rejection
Customer sees nearby alternatives, not a dead end

blocks.title: Interview tip
blocks.text: Say 'outbox plus idempotent consumers' to explain effectively-once delivery without 2PC.

items: 1. `GET /cart` returns items with live prices
2. `POST /checkout/quote` re-validates everything
3. Anything changed? Return a ==diff==, user confirms
4. `POST /orders` with quote_id + idempotency key

caption.text:
"How would you design Swiggy for millions of orders?" 🍔📱

It's one of the most-asked system design interview questions, and most people freeze after drawing three boxes. Here's the full walkthrough, step by step.

What's inside:

1. Problem statement and scope: what you're building, and what you're leaving out
2. Requirements and scale estimates: the numbers that drive every decision
3. High-level architecture: the services and how they talk to each other
4. Restaurant discovery and search: finding food fast, near you
5. Order service and state machine: from placed to delivered, with no stuck orders
6. Cart and checkout: pricing, offers, and keeping the cart consistent
7. Payments: retries, idempotency, and never charging twice
8. Delivery partner assignment: matching the right rider to the right order
9. Real-time tracking and notifications: live location and timely updates
10. Scaling, failure handling and interview questions: what breaks at peak hour, and how to answer follow-ups
